items.explanation: James II created the Dominion after Massachusetts defied the Navigation Acts, placing New England under the iron rule of Sir Edmund Andros, who revoked charters and levied taxes without an assembly.
options: A. Increased democracy in the colonies
B. Strengthened the governor's authority in the region
C. Let New England colonies air common grievances
D. Placed the king in direct control of New England affairs
items.stem: The creation of the Dominion of New England

items.explanation: The 1739 uprising near Charleston terrified planters, who answered with slave codes and harsher discipline meant to deter further revolts.
options: A. A rise in slave imports to the Southern colonies
B. New fortifications around southern cities
C. Efforts to humanize the Middle Passage
D. Harsher treatment of enslaved people across the South

items.explanation: The assemblies alarmed London precisely because they were controlled by colonial elites holding the power of the purse, defying royal instructions and neutering royal governors. They were not democratic bodies — that is the exception.
options: A. Assemblies holding the 'power of the purse' could erode British control
B. Assemblies spread democratic rule through the colonies
C. Assemblies sometimes defied instructions from London
D. Royal governors could barely restrain the assemblies

items.explanation: Under mercantilism the colonies existed to enrich the mother country with raw materials and cash crops — tobacco, rice, indigo, lumber — while buying finished English manufactures.
options: A. To make manufactured goods England preferred not to produce
B. To grow staple crops such as tobacco
C. To supply raw materials such as lumber
D. Both B and C

items.explanation: As the plantation system matured in the 1730s, enslaved laborers were increasingly concentrated on large plantations rather than scattered on small farms, a shift made possible by the booming slave trade after the Dutch lost their monopoly in 1682.
options: A. The Dutch lost their slave-trade monopoly, flooding the colonies with captives
B. Conditions on the Middle Passage grew noticeably milder
C. Enslaved people increasingly lived and worked on large plantations
D. Slave revolts led planters to ease working conditions
items.stem: What change in the southern colonies' slave system began in the 1730s?

items.explanation: The act required colonial goods to ship in English vessels through English ports — textbook mercantilism, the doctrine that a nation's wealth and power grow by controlling trade and accumulating gold and silver.
options: A. Socialism
B. Laissez-faire
C. Progressivism
D. Mercantilism
items.stem: The Navigation Act of 1660 embodied which economic outlook?
items.stimulus:
Questions 6–8 refer to the following excerpt.

"For the increase of shipping and encouragement of the navigation of this nation, wherein, under the good providence and protection of God, the wealth, safety, and strength of this kingdom is so much concerned... no goods or commodities whatsoever shall be imported into or exported out of any lands... belonging to his Majesty... but in such ships as do truly and without fraud belong only to the people of England..."
—Navigation Act of 1660 (abridged)

items.explanation: Parliament passed the act to tighten imperial control over colonial commerce, forcing the tobacco, sugar, and rice trades through English merchants and customs.
options: A. Waning English interest in the American colonies
B. London's drive to tighten control over colonial trade
C. A belief that regulating trade would ruin England
D. Alarm over religious dissenters emigrating to America
